STRUTTING

The Strut Removal Interface: Why It Belongs in the Early Programme

Plan the transition from temporary support to permanent construction.

In this insight

Removal is a project milestoneName the decision makersPlan access for demobilisationClose the documentation loopFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Removal is a project milestone

Temporary support often remains in place while other work progresses around it. Its removal therefore depends on more than the support contractor’s availability. The permanent works, access arrangements and required technical approvals must be coordinated. Place the transition in the master programme early, with named dependencies, rather than treating it as an end-of-package housekeeping activity.

Name the decision makers

Identify who confirms that the relevant conditions for removal have been met, who authorises the operation and who carries it out. The required engineering evidence is project-specific. The commercial team should make sure the contracts support the same responsibility chain. A gap between design responsibility and site authority can create delay precisely when several packages are waiting for access.

Plan access for demobilisation

The site may look very different at removal from how it looked at installation. Review handling space, lifting access and transport routes against the future construction state. Consider whether completed work constrains the planned operation. These questions should be resolved by the relevant specialists during coordination, with any necessary reservations shown on the programme and drawings.

Close the documentation loop

Record the authorised sequence, completion evidence and any retained components or outstanding obligations. Update the handover information so later teams know the current support condition. Commercial close-out should follow the agreed evidence rather than rely on an informal assumption that all temporary work has disappeared. A deliberate transition reduces ambiguity between the temporary support package and the completed basement.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Schedule removal dependencies early.
  • Identify the technical authorisation route.
  • Review demobilisation against the future site layout.
